colour_meaning: Review: one strong sign of risk, or two weaker ones.

items.label: Regional cost factor
items.detail: Prices for similar works in Region IV-A (CALABARZON) run ×1.25 the national median; adjusted for the region: ₱135.6M per km vs national 95th percentile ₱579.0M.

families.name: Contractor ownership, affiliation and bidding networks

items.label: Repeat co-bidders
items.detail: Dqt Builders Corporation and R.T.Y. Construction bid in the same 3 earlier tenders (wins 1–2, alternating).

items.label: Weak: AMO is linked by BetterGov to an elected official (family or earlier term)
items.detail: Philippine Chemsteel Industries, Inc.: AMO Raul S. Cruz. BetterGov analysis, AMO who held office in an earlier term: Raul S. Cruz (Councilor (2007), earlier term). Name match only; verify identity (names are common; the PCAB list gives no birth date).

items.label: Political dynasties in the province (Ateneo dataset)
items.detail: 30% of Quezon's elected local positions were held by fat-dynastic officials after the 2025 election (24% in 1992); median province 28%; largest clan: Alcala (1.6% of positions); family poverty incidence 20% (2012).

items.label: Potential dynasts after the 2025 election (House CPBRD inventory)
items.detail: 57% of elected officials in the province have potential dynastic links (national average 54.5%; broader name matching than the Ateneo measure).

items.label: Political families in the province
items.detail: 0 of 4 elected officials in Quezon (2022-2025) have a relative also in elective office (0%; national median 25%).

items.label: Weak: most of the winner's recent CPES evaluations are behind schedule
items.detail: Philippine Chemsteel Industries, Inc.: of 6 CPES evaluation(s) of its other DPWH contracts in the last 3 years, 2 (33%) were behind schedule. Worst, on 2025-05-06: 3.9% negative slippage during construction (CPES scored schedule 0.111 of 0.15) (contract not stated).

items.label: Winner's other on-going roads
items.detail: Philippine Chemsteel Industries, Inc. has 3 on-going DPWH road(s) possibly stalled and 3 far behind schedule (weekly stage-3 list; DPWH progress data can lag).

items.label: CPES findings on another bidder's recent work
items.detail: R.A. Mendiola Construction & Developer: of 12 CPES evaluation(s) of its other DPWH contracts in the last 3 years, 1 was over the termination threshold, 2 (17%) were behind schedule. Worst, on 2023-09-07: 15% or more negative slippage during construction (CPES scored schedule 0.00 of 0.15; at 15% the procuring entity is required to start termination or take over the work) (contract not stated).

assessment.derivation: 0 strong + 2 weak signal(s) → Medium priority (1 strong, or 2 weak) → Yellow.

steps.title: Confirm the basic facts on the official DPWH page
sub: Budget, location, status, dates and bidders match this page.

steps.title: Open the bid documents
sub: Look for the quantities, a Bill of Quantities and technical specifications.

steps.title: Read Claude's check and confirm its points against the sources
Verify the risk: Political economy and power concentration
sub: Read the source for any company–official link. Political-family context is background only: a family name is never evidence.

If an AMO name matches an official: confirm it is the same person (middle name, age, address, SEC filings) before relying on it. Search the surname on Pulitiklan (pulitiklan.com) and PCIJ's political dynasties database (pcij.org/political-dynasties).
Check the AMO and owners in the firm's SEC filings; the PCAB list names only the AMO.

steps.title: Verify the risk: Implementation delays and performance anomalies
sub: Compare DPWH's reported progress with citizen reports, Bisto.ph inspections and satellite images.

If CPES is cited: open the DPWH quarterly CPES report for that date and confirm the contract, the slippage and the scores. A CPES rating is the agency's own evaluation; ask the district office for the evaluation sheet and the catch-up programme.

steps.title: Check site and field evidence
sub: Check the site before work starts: satellite imagery of the stretch, earlier contracts on the same road, and whether a local monitor (Bisto Proyekto, a TPM civil-society partner) can take geotagged photos later.

steps.title: Write down what you found and keep the documents you relied on
sub: Screenshots, Bill of Quantities pages, photos or letters: attach them with your decision.
